:::{#rem-validation-test-error}
#### What the validation and test errors estimate

The [validation error](#def-validation-error) and the [test error](#def-test-error)
differ from the [training error](#def-training-mse) $\trainerr$ only in the set on which the [fitted model](#def-fitted-model) is evaluated.
The model was not fitted to the validation or [test set](#def-test-set),
so each [estimates](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) the [generalization error](#def-generalization-error) of the fitted model
without the optimism of the training error.
The [validation choice](#def-validation-choice) selects the model with the smallest validation error,
so the validation error of the chosen model is still optimistic;
the test error is computed once, after the choice, so it is not.

@hastie2009elements [sec. 7.2]
use "test error" for the generalization error of the fitted model itself.
Here the test error is the number computed from the test set,
and the generalization error is what it estimates.

Each definition holds for any [loss](#def-observation-loss).
Under squared-error loss, they are sample mean squared errors;
under absolute-error loss, they are sample mean absolute errors.

:::
